analyses.bootstrap: 95% percentile intervals of the duplicate fractions, resampling modules (2,000 resamples, seed 0)
analyses.discordant: tasks proved by exactly one search, per set, with a two-sided sign test

checks.C7: within a task, no goal is drawn twice for the same occurrence

developmentChecksBeforeRegistration: the runner's --develop mode ran both searches with shared draws at 4 expansions on AddConstMapClass.map_const_add, outside the corpus
draws: shared by the two searches of a task (common random numbers): the n-th time a search expands a goal it gets the n-th set of candidates drawn for that goal in this task, whichever search drew it first; goals identified by canonical_goal; so both searches see identical candidates the first time each meets a goal, the AND-OR search (which expands a goal once) only ever uses the first set, and the whole-state search draws afresh on each later expansion of a goal
execution: each unit is one task: the two searches in turn, each in a fresh REPL, whole-state first on tasks of even index and AND-OR first on odd; a unit that raises is recorded as two error rows and run again, both searches with fresh draws, on the next resume; every draw is committed

hypotheses.H50: on the test set, the AND-OR search proves more tasks than the whole-state search (one-sided sign test on the tasks proved by exactly one of them, alpha 0.05)
hypotheses.H51: on the test set, among the tasks both searches prove with different numbers of expansions, the AND-OR search needs fewer in more than half (one-sided sign test, alpha 0.05)
hypotheses.H52: over all tasks, the whole-state search's order-duplicate fraction under the default key is below 1%
hypotheses.H53: on the replication set, the AND-OR search proves at least as many tasks as the whole-state search (H46 of search-v0.5, under shared draws)

measures.draws: per search, the expansions that drew candidates and those that used a set already drawn
measures.entangled: candidates the AND-OR search discarded as entangled
measures.expansionsToProof: the expansion at which a search completed its proof
measures.orderFraction[key]/goalFraction[key]: as search-v0.4, whole-state search, all tasks
measures.proved: tasks with a proof that re-verifies from the statement, per search and set

power: at search-v0.5's rates about a fifth of the statable tasks are proved, so the test set may yield only a handful of discordant tasks and H50 has little power; the decision is reported whichever way it comes out
proposer: as search-v0.5: BFS-Prover-V2-7B in Q8_0, the first goal pretty-printed and followed by ':::', 16 completions at temperature 1.0, at most 64 tokens each, duplicates dropped in order, no menu
question: with a step-level prover as the proposer and its draws shared between the two searches, does a search over goals prove more than a search over whole states
resultsSeenBeforeRegistration: every earlier experiment, including search-v0.5 in full: on the replication set its AND-OR search proved 10 tasks and its whole-state search 8, with 2 proved by the AND-OR search alone; no model search had run on the test set
searches: those of search-v0.4 and v0.5 (search_keys.py), unchanged

tasks.executionOrder: the test set first, then the replication set

sets.test: the 140 tasks after the first 60 of the draw's seeded random order, which no model search has run
